page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-core ARMv9 AWS Graviton4 (Neoverse-V2) processor. Running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, each dedicated physical core maps directly to a single vCPU without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 512.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio (8.0 GB per core). Local storage is not bundled, relying on network-attached storage architectures, and the instance incorporates a high-speed baseline network interface delivering up to 200 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate notable memory throughput and parallel processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth benchmarks place the instance in the top tier, delivering 479.59 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 235.55 GB/sec on large-block writes. Multithreaded execution is similarly robust, achieving top-tier scores in Geekbench multi-core (25460.0), Clang software compilation (81149.0), PassMark database operations (48122.38), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (673.46 GB/sec). Furthermore, in-memory caching performance is exceptionally high, measured at 133.96 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

Performance profiles exhibit distinct tradeoffs between multi-threaded scale and per-core execution. While multi-threaded compute and throughput tests consistently rank in the top quartile, single-core benchmarks—including stress-ng single-core (1706.49) and Geekbench single-core (1891.0)—remain in the middle 50% tier. Small-model LLM text generation shows lower relative throughput (26.8 tokens/sec), whereas larger models demonstrate stronger relative multi-core execution (41.29 tokens/sec on 7B and 6.0 tokens/sec on 70B models).

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of the Graviton4 ARM architecture combined with 200 Gbps networking and an expansive memory pool, minimizing the hardware footprint required for memory-intensive environments. The lack of attached local NVMe drives requires external provisioning for persistent volumes, but the memory density and network interface support large distributed datasets. Workloads best aligned with the r8gn.16xlarge profile include in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise relational databases, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated arm64 cores based on the AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 architecture clocked at 2.8 GHz. It delivers 512.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per vCPU) and a baseline network throughput of 200 Gbps, operating without bundled local storage or integrated GPUs. Evaluated benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded and memory bandwidth performance, including 479.59 GB/sec uncached memory reads, 133.96 million Redis SET operations per second, and leading multi-core Geekbench and database operation results. Single-thread processing registers in the middle performance tier. The instance provides high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound systems by consolidating massive RAM capacity and high-throughput networking into an efficient ARM platform, making it particularly suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, distributed analytics, and enterprise data processing.
